totals.check: 1850 labour + 590 materials = 2440 scope subtotal, access excluded

derivation.rationale: REFUSED. Dan stated he has not contacted a rental yard. The tool will not manufacture a figure for the largest cost in the job. A call sheet is produced instead, specifying the machine class and the site constraints to quote against.
Not a rate card item. Added because the access route is finished landscaping rather than a driveway, and damage to it is foreseeable. Cheaper as a priced line than as an argument at final invoice.

Priced at the historic NHL lime rate (historic.nhl_lime_repointing, $16–28/sq ft) rather than the general fieldstone repoint rate (stone.fieldstone_repoint, $18–30/sq ft), because pre-1930 construction — if confirmed — mandates lime mortar. $25/sq ft, upper-middle: solo working from a platform is slower than working from staging. THE AREA IS INVENTED. An assumed 11 ft perimeter over the top 4 ft. Nobody measured the chimney, and 'absolutely massive' suggests the assumption may be low. This is the single largest guess in the estimate and it is the first thing the site visit settles.

Dan could not establish the count from the ground and said so. The tool carries the uncertainty forward as an allowance of three units at mid-band ($230 each) rather than resolving it into a false number. Billed as performed; each additional unit is $120–350.

Revised DOWN after Dan confirmed a cap is present and looks intact. The earlier allowance assumed the top might be open and need closing. Priced near the low end: verification and sealing, not construction. Kept in scope because the lift is already on site — returning for a $350 seal means paying the access cost twice.

project_name: Stone chimney — upper section crack repair

model.recommendation: Day rate. Not per square foot.
model.why: Small quantity of masonry, large quantity of getting to it: most of the labour is positioning a machine and carrying stone.

range.equipment_note: Lift rental — nobody has quoted it yet.

scope_sentence: Rake and repoint the failed joints in the upper section of the stone chimney, reset shifted units, and seal the top against water entry. Chimney remains out of service.

objections.objection: Why not just patch the crack from a ladder?
objections.response: Over twenty feet with stone already shifted, a ladder gives you one hand and nowhere to hold a unit while you bed it.
objections.grounded_in: Memo: 20+ ft, stones appear to have shifted

objections.objection: Can you use regular mortar? It is cheaper.
objections.response: Pre-1930 stone takes Type N or NHL lime. Portland is harder than the stone and spalls the face — you would be repairing the repair.

objections.objection: The chimney does not even work. Why spend anything?
objections.response: It is enclosed by the house. If the upper section keeps moving, what it comes down onto is roof and interior, not lawn.

next_steps: Measure on site: path width at its narrowest, truck to chimney, height, ground condition.
Call a rental yard: weekly rate, stowed width, rack capacity, delivery, damage waiver.
tax_action: Add sales tax to the whole invoice — every line here is a taxable repair, including the lift when it is billed on.
